newsitem.title: UK: British Gas claims subsea drilling record.
newsitem.headline: British Gas claims subsea drilling record.

text.p: British Gas Exploration and Production (E&P) is claiming a world record for the longest well to be drilled by a semi-submersible rig.
The well, the eighth to be drilled at the Armada project in the Central North Sea, operated by British Gas E&P, is 23,905 feet (over 4.5 miles) long.
British Gas said in a statement that the well is inclined at an angle of 74.4 degrees from vertical, covers a total horizontal distance of over 20,000 feet and reaches a vertical depth of 9,148 feet.
Colin Friedlander, Technical Director of British Gas E&P, said that the well is more than 1,500 feet longer than the previous record, set by the Ocean Rover in the Gulf of Mexico in 1985.

The Armada project will gather gas and associated liquids from three fields, Drake, Fleming and Hawkins. Output is expected to reach 450 million standard cubic feet a day of gas and 26,000 barrels per day of oil when production starts in October 1997.

Partners in the project are British Gas E&P, operator, 46.27 percent; Amoco (UK) Exploration Company, 18.20 percent; Fina Exploration Limited, 11.53 percent; Phillips Petroleum Company United Kingdom Ltd, 11.45 percent; Yorkshire Energy Ltd, 6.97 percent; and Agip (UK) Ltd, 5.58 percent.
